Running new lines from the front of the ship to the back was difficult in the sense that it was just plain awkward, the heath shielding underneath had to come off in a special pattern to keep from being damaged. Not that they were particularly fragile, the composite plates were incredibly lightweight and quite sturdy, but prying on one could cause issues. Then came the damned insulation, he had to wear an EVA suit for that to keep from catching a hundred kinds of cancer! Still, it went fine and he freed up a channel down to the bare metal of the structural hull where the pipes could go; a few tack welds on their braces kept them in place.

This new set of pipes would help the life support system do it's job to keep the air fresh and clean, but most importantly it would boost the system's efficiency in reducing and reforming the molecules in the atmospheric gases. An excellent addition, in Stan's opinion.

This was a critical aspect for any "frontier vessel" that often sat on the ground for weeks, months, perhaps even years at a time and served as a home and workshop for settlers. Even on inhabited planets it was popular to just park a ship somewhere, sometimes among clusters of other ships, and just live right out of it rather than build a more permanent settlement. Some ships were purpose-built for this and were only as aerodynamic as they had to be, and were only capable of small FTL hops that likely wouldn't be able to take them anywhere useful.

Waylander class vessels did not have that problem, they were developed by a nation that hadn't participated in wider galactic affairs and had little use for any of that. When Seylonis was colonized it was done so by a population of science and military-oriented individuals, they took several Earth cultures with them from the North American and European continents. Of course they valued individual liberty, but the true virtue of their citizens were the dual traits of preparedness and community; rarely did they do anything alone. Waylanders weren't designed to "settle" anywhere on their own but could do it in a pinch, it was the Charlestown class landers that would do the bulk of the work.

Somewhere out there, he had forgotten where exactly, was a whole fleet of them hidden safely away on some lifeless rock. During the final days of the war they were squirreled away like so many other "critical assets" that couldn't be easily moved.

Someday they would be reclaimed. He made his pact with the devil to live long enough to make it happen.

A lifetime ago Stan had found the Kriegsmark in the hands of some tired old mercenary who lost it in a card game, the man had been part of the much maligned SDFNS Scout Corps that was regarded as the "bastard stepchild of the navy." They were the people who went out and set down somewhere to put down nav beacons and keep the charts up to date, spending countless hours measuring gravitational waves and magnetic fields and who the hell knows what else. When the Kriegsmark was laid down she was meant to be the home away from home for the crews of her close cousins, so the equipment she had was best suited for keeping things running way the hell out there.

Most of her life support and "mission support" equipment was still in working order, but it was the "gas cracker" that really needed some help. Waste heat from the fusion reactors wasn't easy to get since they were designed to be as absolutely efficient as possible, so whatever was captured would have to be enough for the processes.

Except Stan wanted more! Over in the nose of the aircraft, right above the torpedo racks, the ship had a pair of small heat exchangers that had been part of an older system and remained unused. With the loop hooked up the system could then generate incredibly high temperature steam that would be mixed with CO2 to create formate, which was the anion of formic acid and could be used in other chemical processes or in a formic acid fuel cell. There were also several methods to produce methane, toulene, and other hydrocarbons that had obvious usage as fuel or explosives; toulene in particular was the precursor agent to trinitrotoluene or more commonly known as TNT.

None of that actually improved the ability to actually scrub the CO2 from the ship's atmosphere which was crucial, but if needed the water on board could be reduced to O2 and H2 and then sent to the atmosphere loop and the fuel processor.

That was last resort stuff, regular H2 didn't quite have the same potency as using lithium and deuterium but unfortunately only the really advanced reactors could utilize lithium-6 like that. Inside the Kriegsmark were two sets of two tanks, one for tritium and the other for deuterium, and this reaction produced more than enough energy for the ship. Regular hydrogen cut from water was a terrible choice for the reactor, but he didn't quite understand why that was and nor did he care.

Testing the system would mean flying fast enough which wasn't possible at the moment, most of his poor ship's exterior was scattered around in the grass or stacked up in clumsy piles. Seeing her in such a state made him feel awkward, the only things he hadn't torn off were the panels around the "through-hull devices" such as windows or the turrets, the nacelle panels, and the flight surfaces along the wings and fuselage. Some of the air brakes had been extended which made the Kriegsmark look like an angry bird that just discovered some asshole had defeathered her, at least he could smirk at that.
